description: Hello folks! My name is Michael Wilde, I'm a 38 year old Engineer and hobbyist software developer working in Agriculture (mainly Dairy). I'm a huge NASA fan and as soon as I saw this challenge, knew it was for me! I want to utilize NASA Technology and Data sets to make something genuinely useful and reliable to help Farmers both Locally, and worldwide farm as efficiently and as cost effective as possible. NASA powered Agriculture.
summary: In short: a farmer taps a field and answers four questions, and Harvest Star tests their crop rotation against every season NASA has measured over that field since 1984. The NASA weather is calibrated with Met Éireann's local records and costed with Teagasc figures, and the results come back as three plain options.
details:
Harvest Star is a decision-support app for tillage farmers, built for the Field Shift challenge. A farmer taps their field on a satellite map and enters the last three crops, drainage, soil test results and what matters most to them: profit, less fertiliser, soil health or low risk. The app then compares their current rotation with two alternatives. It replays each option through every season NASA has recorded for that field since 1984.

Each option gets risk ratings for weather, disease, buyers and season, along with figures for money, nitrogen and sowing. Farmers can also test a wetter autumn, a wetter spring or a drier year. A “What’s changed” screen compares the early and recent halves of the field’s record, showing how sowing days, drought and temperature have shifted.

The weather data comes from NASA’s POWER API, which is based on MERRA-2 and CERES. Harvest Star tunes it with Met Éireann rainfall data and checks it against the Mullingar station, then combines it with Teagasc costs and sowing windows and the Irish nitrogen rules. The result is advice that holds up locally for farmers around Athlone and across Ireland. It suggests options to explore and leaves the decision to the farmer.
